title: Lesson 7 - Grounding Techniques: What Grounds a Prompt and Where It Lives
description: Given a scenario, identify the appropriate grounding technique.

questions.question: An agent must answer policy questions from a library of Knowledge articles, matching on meaning rather than exact keywords. Which grounding technique fits?
options: A merge field that pulls the article title onto the case
A Flow resource that copies the article body onto the record
A Data 360 retriever that indexes the articles and returns the most relevant chunks at run time
An Apex resource that concatenates every article into one field
questions.explanation: A Data 360 retriever indexes unstructured content and performs semantic search over it, returning relevant chunks to the LLM, which is retrieval augmented generation and the right tool for meaning-based matching over a corpus.

questions.question: A reply must always name the customer's account status, a field that already exists on the Contact record. Which grounding technique fits?
options: A merge field that references the record field
A vector retriever over the account documents
An ensemble retriever across all data sources
A prompt flow that recomputes the status from scratch
questions.explanation: A merge field pulls a known field value deterministically and cheaply from the associated record, so a value that already sits on the Contact is a merge field job rather than a retrieval job.

questions.question: Before the agent writes a reply, a discount value must be computed from purchase history on a different object. Which grounding technique fits?
options: A merge field on the Contact record
A Data Library over uploaded files
A vector search index over the history text
A Flow or Apex resource used to ground the prompt with the computed value
questions.explanation: When a value must be computed or fetched across objects before the prompt is built, a Flow or Apex resource grounds the template with that value, whereas merge fields only reach fields on the associated record.
